text.p: Telecom Italia said on Thursday it was launching a "supercordless" telephone that will boost the reception of ordinary domestic cordless phones, enabling users to take their home telephone out and about on long distances.
Telecom managing director Francesco Chirichigno said the group was investing 1.8 billion lire in the phone, to be called "Fido", and estimated it would have a million customers by 1998.

"The technology is similar to that of normal cordless phones which now work in a range of 200 metres (yards)," he told a news conference. "With this new service it will be possible to take your home phone with you when you go into town."
The phone would keep the user's home telephone number.
Chirichigno said he did not believe the new phone would lure customers away from ordinary analogue mobile phones, since users tended to upgrade from those to GSM (digital) technology.
"Fido" -- which means "I trust" in Italian and is a popular English dog's name -- will be launched near Christmas in five Italian cities and will be expanded to all major cities in 1997.
